`isoparse('1970-01-01T00:00:00.851')` returns a datetime whose microsecond
field is 851 instead of 851000: the fraction is being read as whole
microseconds rather than as a decimal fraction of a second. Inputs with more

`dt_to_timestamp` must return the correct epoch seconds for these fractional
ISO-8601 timestamps once parsing is fixed.

Fix the ISO-8601 fractional-second handling in `boltons/timeutils.py`.

## Issue

The ISO-8601 parser `isoparse` mishandles fractional seconds.

`isoparse('1970-01-01T00:00:00.851')` returns a datetime whose microsecond
field is 851 instead of 851000: the fraction is being read as whole
microseconds rather than as a decimal fraction of a second. Inputs with more
than six fractional digits (for example `.123456789`) raise
`ValueError: microsecond must be in 0..999999` instead of truncating to
microsecond precision.

`dt_to_timestamp` must return the correct epoch seconds for these fractional
ISO-8601 timestamps once parsing is fixed.

Fix the ISO-8601 fractional-second handling in `boltons/timeutils.py`.

  66| def dt_to_timestamp(dt):
  67|     """Converts from a :class:`~datetime.datetime` object to an integer
  68|     timestamp, suitable interoperation with :func:`time.time` and
  69|     other `Epoch-based timestamps`.
  70| 
  71|     .. _Epoch-based timestamps: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time
  72| 
  73|     >>> timestamp = int(time.time())
  74|     >>> utc_dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(timestamp, timezone.utc)
  75|     >>> timestamp - dt_to_timestamp(utc_dt)
  76|     0.0
  77| 
  78|     ``dt_to_timestamp`` supports both timezone-aware and naïve
  79|     :class:`~datetime.datetime` objects. Note that it assumes naïve
  80|     datetime objects are implied UTC, such as those generated with
  81|     :meth:`datetime.datetime.utcnow`. If your datetime objects are
  82|     local time, such as those generated with
  83|     :meth:`datetime.datetime.now`, first convert it using the
  84|     :meth:`datetime.datetime.replace` method with ``tzinfo=``
  85|     :class:`LocalTZ` object in this module, then pass the result of
  86|     that to ``dt_to_timestamp``.
  87| 
  88|     A datetime is naïve when its :meth:`~datetime.datetime.utcoffset`
  89|     returns ``None``, even if it has a ``tzinfo`` object.
  90|     """
  91|     if dt.utcoffset() is not None:
  92|         td = dt - EPOCH_AWARE
  93|     else:
  94|         td = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) - EPOCH_AWARE
